result:
**I'd eliminate the instinct for humans to dehumanize each other.**

If I could change only one thing, it would be to remove our species' wired tendency to divide into "us" versus "them" — the psychological shortcut that lets us justify cruelty, exploitation, indifference, and violence the moment we stop seeing the other person as fully human.

Everything else we fight about (resources, ideology, power, revenge, status) becomes dramatically less destructive when that single cognitive bug is patched out. 

We would still disagree. We would still compete. We would still have conflicting interests. But we would argue, negotiate, and even fight while instinctively recognizing the other side as fully real, fully conscious, and equally valuable. The intellectual and moral floor would rise overnight.

No more industrialized indifference to suffering. No more casual othering that scales into atrocities. No more "they're not like us" mentalities that make slavery, genocide, caste systems, or casual bigotry feel natural.

The world wouldn't become utopia. It would become a place where our remaining flaws have much less room to grow into horrors.

That single change feels like the highest-leverage edit I could make to human nature. Everything downstream gets better.
